Actor.description:
Who made the write (0.5). `run` and `phase` are reserved now so that writes a run makes need no later schema
change. They are not tied to a kind: a workflow op inside a run may carry `run`, and an agent outside a run,
such as one whose actor is read from the process tree, may have neither.

AgentEvent.description:
One normalized event of an agent session (0.3, Normalized events).

Every known event is a closed object: an unknown key is an error. An event whose `type` this version does not
know (a tool's newer stream, an event of a later Collide) reads as [`AgentEvent::Other`] with that name in
`raw_type` and the rest of the object in `raw`, because a log line must stay readable. `Other` is also what an
adapter emits for a stream event it does not map. It is written back as `{"type":"other","raw_type":...}`, so a
read-write-read is stable. The schema lists the known events only.

oneOf.description: A message of the agent, or one chunk of it.
A tool call. `input` is `None` while the agent has not sent it.
The request had no option Collide may pick, so the session answered `cancel` (0.3, Permissions).
The session id is known: at once for Claude, on the `session/new` response for ACP.
`empty` is true when the turn gave no message, no tool call and zero or unreported usage.

The account's usage limit is reached (0.3, Usage and rate limits). `reset_at_ms` is the wall-clock time it
resets, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, and is absent when the tool does not say. Only an adapter with
`limit_signal` reports it.

One hook call: its name (`PreToolUse:Bash`), the event it hooked (`PreToolUse`), how it ended, its exit code and
the `decision` its output gave, when it gave one. The hook's `stdout` and `stderr` are untrusted text that may
hold secrets, so the event has no place for them (0.3, The stream protocol).

A tool hook failed (`cause`) and the call it hooked, `tool_call_id`, ran anyway: a guard that did not guard
(0.13). It is what a session can know about the detector; the finding, with its cost, is the metrics item's.
A tool call that did not run, by the id of the [`AgentEvent::ToolCall`], and who refused it.

The size in bytes of a tool call's result, by the id of the [`AgentEvent::ToolCall`] (0.13, the token and context
metrics). It is given for every result, a refused call's included. The result's content is untrusted and may be
large, so the event holds the size and nothing else.
An event this version has no type for. `raw_type` is its own type name.

Batch.description: One call on several items fires per item; `index` counts from 0.

BudgetScope.description: The budget that stopped a run: the run's total, a phase's, or a role's (0.7, Budgets).

Category.description: The category every source status maps to, so views and columns work across sources (0.10).

Change.description:
The `change` a task point carries. `op` is null for a write made by a run (`via: run`). `from` is null at
create and `to` is null at delete. `diff` is predicted at `before_*` and actual at `after_*`. `effectOf` is the
key of the item whose op changed this one.

Effect.description: One item that an op changed: an entry of `apply`'s and `preview`'s `items[]`.

Event.description:
One line of the event log. `wall_ms` is the wall clock in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. `experiment` is null
outside an experiment (0.4).

EventBody.description: What happened. Each variant is one event name, and `event` is the tag. Unknown keys are refused.

oneOf.description: `from` is null for the first state.

The phase's log and transcript paths are carried, because a registry needs them (0.4). A `human` phase has no
log, only agent phases have a transcript, and a phase entering its first state has neither yet, so both are
null until they exist. `round` counts the phase's repeats, as `HookPhase.round` does.

`run` is null for a gate on a named point that no run is running. A gate sits on a phase (`phase`) or on a
named point (`point`, 0.4 Gates). `message` is the hook's own message, as in `HookResult.message`.

`cause` names the decision token, the budget, or the agent's stop-and-report that led to the question.
`queue_item` is the Queue item the run waits on (0.13), so an answer matches its question.
A write Collide made. `key` names the item; the change says what it did.

Written before the step. `action` says what the step will do. After a restart, an intent with no outcome is
checked against the world, never repeated blind (0.2).

Written after the step, with the same `step` and `kind`. `result` says how it ended; `detail` says more, such as
the merge commit or the PR url.

FailCause.description:
Why a phase failed when the cause is known. A phase that ends with no `result` on a full volume fails with cause
`disk`, not `lost` (0.2).

FieldDiff.description:
One changed field: `{from, to}`, or `{added, removed}` for a set. `from` is null at create and `to` is null
at delete.

FinalReportSource.description:
Where a [`AgentEvent::FinalReport`] came from: Claude's `result` field, or, for ACP, the message chunks after the
last tool call.

HookDecision.description:
What a hook's own output decided, read from the `decision` it printed (0.3, The stream protocol). Only this word is
kept: the output itself may hold secrets. `block` is a `PostToolUse` hook's, which leaves the tool's result as it was.

HookExperiment.description: Inside an experiment: the experiment, the arm and the arm's directory, so a hook can skip a push (0.14).

HookFailure.description: How a hook that was meant to guard a tool call failed without stopping it (0.13, the failed-open detector).

oneOf.description: The hook exited with a code that is neither 0 nor the deliberate block, 2 (S9: exit 1).
The hook timed out, so it gave no verdict.

HookOutcome.description:
How a hook call ended, as the agent reports it (S9: `success`, `error` for an exit other than 0, `cancelled` for a
timeout).

HookStatus.description:
The verdict a hook writes. It is `ok`, `fail`, `unverified` (could not check here), `pending` (has not happened
yet), `refused` or `error`. `unverified` and `pending` are valid only from some hooks: see [`effective_result`].

ItemState.description: An item's status and its category.

Money.description: An amount in a currency. Claude reports USD.

OutputEntry.description:
One normalized event of an agent's stream, with its place in the phase's log and the time the shim saw it (from
the journal's `wall_ns`, so a replayed log gives the same time). `index` counts from 0 in the phase instance's log.

PauseCause.description:
Why a run or a phase is paused (0.2, 0.3, 0.8). `ask_human` waits in the Queue, `usage_limit` waits for the
account's reset time, and `disk` is the free-space floor: nothing is started until space comes back (0.2).

PermissionAnswer.description: The answer to a permission request (0.3, S7).

PermissionOption.description: One of the agent's own options in a permission request.

PermissionOptionKind.description:
The kind of one of the agent's own options in a permission request. Collide picks only the `*_once` kinds: the
agent owns the scope and storage of an "always" choice, so no adapter selects one (0.3, Permissions).

PermissionRequest.description:
A request to run a tool (0.3, Permissions). `input` is `None` when the agent has not sent it yet (opencode sends
`rawInput: {}` for a Bash call, so the command is unknown until the host answers; S7). Such a request shows in the
Queue as "input not available until approved" and no pack rule that reads the input may auto-allow it.
`reason` says why it was asked, when the agent says. `options` are the agent's own.

PhaseState.description:
Where a phase is (0.8, Phase). A shim that dies without an `exit.json` makes its phase `lost`, whatever the agent's
stream said (0.2).

Point.description:
The point catalogue (0.4, Named points), in the table's order. Serialized as its dotted name. Adding a point is
a schema change: `Point.input.json` lists the names.

QueueChanged.description:
The params of the `queue.changed` notification: the Queue's size after a change and the items that came and went,
so a badge or a menu needs no other message. A client lists the Queue with `queue.list` for the rest.

RefusalCause.description:
Who refused a tool call, or why it did not run (0.3, The stream protocol). The adapter reads it from the tool's own
metadata and never from the result's text. `unknown` is any other shape of refusal.

oneOf.description: A hook denied it.
Collide's own `deny` answer.
A permission rule, or an automatic deny.
The session does not have the tool.

Rename.description:
An id that changed, at Share or `renumber`. It is also the body of the provider's `task.renamed`
notification, which names the `checkout`; inside a `change`, the change's own `checkout` applies.

ReportLine.description:
One report line. Every line carries `v` and its timestamp `t`, because a time stamped at reading would be wrong
by the tailing lag. Each variant repeats `v` and `t`: serde cannot flatten them out of a tagged enum that denies
unknown keys. A key a reporter does not know is left out, and shows as "not reported" (0.13).

oneOf.description:
Keeps `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` apart, and may split `cacheWrite` into `cacheWrite1h` and `cacheWrite5m`.
A merged `cached` count is rejected: a write and a read are priced far apart.
`resetsAt` is the reset time in epoch seconds.

RunOutputNotice.description:
The params of the `run.output` notification: one new entry of a phase's stream, sent to a connection that has
subscribed to events (`daemon.subscribe`).

RunState.description:
Where a run is (0.8, Run). It ends `ended(<outcome>)`, `failed` or `stopped`; `outcome` is the `end` token the run
reached (0.7, Outcomes and terminal states). `integrating` is a run whose `integrate` answered `pending`, so the
pull request is not merged yet (0.4).

RunTerminalOutput.description: The params of the `run.terminal_output` notification: bytes the take-over's terminal wrote, as base64.

StepKind.description:
The side-effect steps that write an intent before and an outcome after (0.2): an integrate, a source op, an
`after_integrate` hook and a remote write.

StepResult.description: How a side-effect step ended. A merge that finds its change already at the target is `succeeded` (0.2).

TaskChanged.description:
`task.changed`. `from` is null at create and `to` is null at delete, as in `change`. `actor` is the source's
own, when it knows it (GitHub events, the beads journal); `automated` is GitHub's `wasAutomated`.

checkout.description: The checkout whose copy changed, for a ref-scoped source; absent for a global source (such as GitHub).

TaskInvalid.description:
`task.invalid`: something the source could not read as a task. Core turns it into a Queue item. `checkout` is
null for a source that is not ref-scoped.

checkout.description: The checkout whose copy was removed, for a ref-scoped source; absent for a global source (such as GitHub).

ToolKind.description:
What a tool call does, as the agent classifies it. Adapters classify by `kind` and input, never by a call's title
(S7, O12).

TurnEndReason.description:
Why a turn ended (0.3, A turn ends with). `error` carries the HTTP status of an API failure when there is one
(S1 measured a 429). `blocked` is a prompt a `UserPromptSubmit` hook refused: the turn never ran, and `reason` is
the hook's own, when it gave one (S9). The result that follows it is the hook's message, never the phase's report.

oneOf.description: The role's budget ran out (Claude's `error_max_budget_usd`). The phase pauses rather than fails (0.3).

Usage.description:
What an agent spent (0.3, Usage). Every number is an `Option`: a figure the agent did not report is `None`, never
0, and is left out of the JSON. `cache_write_1h` and `cache_write_5m` split `cache_write` by tier, where the tool
reports the tiers (capability `usage_report.cache_write_tiers`). `model_time_ms` is the time the model call or calls
took, when the agent reports it (0.13: a turn's is a difference of a running total).

UsageQuality.description:
How far the figures of a [`Usage`] event can be trusted. A total built from `partial` figures is shown as "at
least" and never summed with `exact` ones (0.13).

UsageScope.description:
What a [`Usage`] event counts: one turn, one model step, the session so far, a compaction call, or another model call
outside the turn's own (0.3, Usage).

oneOf.description:
The model call of a compaction. A turn's own usage leaves it out, so it is its own event, never added into a
`Turn` (0.3, Usage; S9).

A model call that is neither the turn's own nor a compaction: a helper-model call, read as what the agent
reports for the turn beyond the turn's own usage. Never added into a `Turn` either.

WorkspaceState.description:
Where a workspace is (0.8, Workspace): `provisioning → ready → in_use → idle → removable → removed`, plus
`failed`, which resumes through the `resume` hook.

description:
What the daemon sends without being asked, after `daemon.subscribe`. On the wire a notice is a [`Notification`]
whose `method` is the name below and whose `params` is the payload.

oneOf.description: An event of the store, with its `seq` and the actor the daemon recorded.
One new entry of a phase's normalized stream.
Bytes a take-over's terminal wrote.
The Queue changed.
